image_description: Two identical black, vertical tower-style computer speakers standing side-by-side against a white background. Each speaker features a glossy black rectangular enclosure with rounded corners. The top section has a silver/metallic mesh grille covering the tweeter area. Below that is a small circular driver (mid-range or tweeter). The bottom half appears to be a solid glossy panel, possibly hiding a larger woofer or serving as a passive radiator/base. There is white text branding near the bottom of each speaker.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The objects are clearly rectangular prisms with rounded edges, fitting the 'box-shaped' description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: One or more circular speaker cones on front face of varying sizes.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Each speaker has at least one visible circular driver element in the upper-middle section. The lower section is ambiguous but consistent with a sealed enclosure design.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Prominent large woofer dominating the front face with a much smaller tweeter positioned above or beside it.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: This specific configuration (large dominant woofer + small tweeter) is NOT present. These appear to be satellite speakers with a small mid-driver and a top-mounted tweeter array, lacking a large visible woofer cone on the front face.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Cone surface made of paper, polypropylene, or composite with rubber surround.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The resolution is insufficient to definitively identify the material composition (paper vs plastic) or the rubber surround texture of the small visible driver.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Grille cloth or perforated metal may cover the drivers.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The top section of each speaker clearly features a perforated metal or mesh grille structure.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Terminal connections visible on rear panel.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image shows only the front view; the rear panel is completely occluded.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Wood, MDF, or plastic enclosure with black, white, or wood-grain finish.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The enclosure has a high-gloss black finish, consistent with painted MDF or plastic commonly used for computer speakers.
The visual features (drivers, grille, enclosure shape) strongly identify these as audio output devices.

artifact_observations.location: Bottom front face of both speakers
artifact_observations.reasoning: The white branding text at the bottom is illegible and distorted. It resembles letters but does not form coherent words, a common AI artifact where text generation fails.
The mesh pattern on the top grilles is inconsistent and slightly 'melted' or irregular, lacking the precise geometric repetition of real manufactured perforated metal.
The reflections on the glossy black body are vague and do not correspond to a clear light source or environment, appearing slightly smeared rather than sharp.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific type of speaker (computer satellite vs studio monitor) and verify class alignment.
To analyze the illegible text artifacts at the bottom of the speakers and determine if they are nonsensical gibberish.
To check for edge bleeding between the glossy black speaker and the white background, and ensure the grille is properly connected to the body.

focus_areas: Legibility and structure of the white text at the bottom
Geometric regularity of the top mesh grille pattern
Consistency of reflections on the glossy black surface
Boundary sharpness between speaker and background
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the text at the bottom. AI often generates 'fake' logos that look like text from a distance but are gibberish up close. Also, inspect the top grille: real perforated metal has a uniform grid; AI often warps this pattern. Check if the small circular driver looks physically mounted or just painted on.
